title_en: The Legend of the New Year
full_text_zh:
[P1] 中国老故事
过年的传说
林晓慧 编著 张子剑 编绘
桉恺绘本馆
北方妇女儿童出版社
·长春·

[P2] 相传，古时候有一只大怪兽叫作“年”。
它头上长着角，牙齿又尖又锋利，眼睛大如铜铃，
目光凶狠，看起来非常可怕！

“年”常年居住在海底的深处。每到除夕这天，
它就会爬上岸，来到人类居住的地方。
它实在太大了，每爬一步，大地都会跟着震动！

[P3] 大家都吓坏了！
所以，每逢除夕，村里的男女老少都跑到
深山老林里藏起来，躲避“年”的追杀。

“年”到了岸上，像疯了一样，张开血盆大口，
就开始吞食生命。
从小昆虫到大活人，它一个也不放过。

[P4] 有一年除夕，桃花村的乡亲们正忙着收拾行李，
上山避难。
人们封锁门窗，牵着牛，赶着羊，匆匆忙忙离开家。
路上，青年男女抱着小孩，扶着老人，神情很恐慌。
这时，村外来了个
乞讨的老人。他拄着拐
杖，背着袋子，眼睛炯炯
有神，银白色的胡须在
风中飘扬。

[P5] 一位老婆婆从家里出来，送给老人一些食物，对他说：“老人家，你也快上山吧！怪兽‘年’就要来啦！
老人捋了捋胡须，笑着说：“婆婆，你要是让我在你家住一晚，我一定能把‘年’赶跑！”，

[P6] “别开玩笑了，‘年’很凶残的，你斗不过它，
快逃命吧！”老婆婆继续劝说。
可是，老人却笑而不语。
老婆婆无奈地摇摇头，只
好回家拿上行李，加入上山的
队伍，留下老人独自在家。

[P7] 寒风呼啸，天越来越黑。
到了半夜，“年”大吼一声，
猛地闯进村里来。
“年”隐约感觉，村里的气氛
有些不一样。它一抬头，发现老婆
婆家门口，贴着大红纸。
它看了一眼，身子竟然抖了一下，还发出了一声怪叫。

[P8] “年”赶紧把目光移开，望向屋内。
谁知，屋子里点满了蜡烛，充满了光明。
这片光深深刺痛了“年”的眼睛。

“年”心想：“这家搞的什么把戏，竟敢戏弄本兽！
看我不把你们通通吃掉！”
于是，它瞪着眼睛，狂叫着扑过去。

[P9] “噼里啪啦！”
说时迟，那时快。
屋里的老人，点燃一串鞭炮，扔了出去。
鞭炮在空中划出一道优美的弧线，正好
落在“年”的头顶上。
“噼里啪啦！”
正当“年”要闯进门时，鞭炮在它头上炸开了花。
一阵疼痛袭来，浓浓的烟雾遮住了它的双眼。

[P10] “年”见到红色，全身抖了起来。
它见势不妙，三步一踉跄，连滚带爬地逃走了。
“年”吓了一大跳，不敢冒然向前冲了。
等浓烟散去，它发现，门竟然打开了。
“哈哈哈……”院子里站着一位身穿大红袍的老人，
正大声笑着。

[P11] 乡亲们高兴极了，纷纷穿上新衣服，
戴上新帽子，到亲戚朋友家相互道喜。
大年初一，人们从山上回来。
大家惊奇地发现，村里的一切
都完好无损。

[P12] 这时，老婆婆想起了乞讨老人的话，
恍然大悟。
她对乡亲们说起此事，大家都觉得
很神奇。

人们纷纷跑到老婆婆家里，想看个究竟。
他们发现，老婆婆家的门上，贴着红纸。
屋里，点满了发光的红蜡烛。院子里还有一堆
没烧完的鞭炮，正在“噼啪”作响。

[P13] “看来，‘年’很怕红色。”
“没错，它还很怕光！”
“鞭炮的响声，可以把它赶跑！”
大家议论纷纷，找出了驱赶“年”的办法。
从此，每年除夕，家家户户都会在门上贴红对联，
在门口放响亮的鞭炮。
吉祥如意
五湖四海皆春色
万水千山尽

[P14] 除夕的夜晚，家人们会聚在一起，
吃年夜饭，在家里点上灯烛，一晚上都不灭。
光把家里照得亮堂堂的，“年”
兽再也不敢来了。
大年初一，人们还要走亲访友，相互拜年，
传达问候和祝福。
后来，这些习俗越传越广，就演变成了中
国民间最热闹、最隆重的春节。
full_text_en:
[P1] Chinese Old Stories
The Legend of the New Year
Compiled and written by Lin Xiaohui, Illustrated by Zhang Zijian
Ankai Picture Book House
Northeastern Women and Children's Publishing House
·Changchun·

[P2] It is said that long ago, there was a huge monster called 'Nian'.
It had horns on its head, sharp and pointed teeth, eyes as big as bronze bells,
and fierce, terrifying eyes!

'Nian' lived deep in the ocean. Every New Year's Eve,
it would crawl ashore to the places where humans lived.
It was so huge that every step it took made the earth tremble!

[P3] Everyone was terrified!
So, every New Year's Eve, the men, women, old and young in the village would run to the deep mountains and forests to hide, escaping the monster 'Nian's' pursuit.

When 'Nian' reached the shore, it went wild, opened its huge, bloodthirsty mouth,
and began devouring life.
From tiny insects to living people, it spared no one.

[P4] One New Year's Eve, the villagers of Taohua Village were busy packing their belongings and heading to the mountains to escape the disaster.
People locked their doors and windows, led their cattle, herded their sheep, and hurriedly left home.
On the road, young men and women carried children and supported the elderly, their expressions full of fear.
At this moment, an old beggar came from outside the village. He leaned on a cane, carried a bag, had bright, alert eyes, and his silvery beard fluttered in the wind.

[P5] An old woman came out of her house, gave the old man some food, and said to him: "Old man, you should hurry up and go to the mountains! The monster 'Nian' is coming!

The old man stroked his beard and smiled: "Grandma, if you let me stay at your house for one night, I'm sure I can drive away 'Nian'!"

[P6] "Don't joke around, 'Nian' is very fierce, you can't beat it, 
run for your life!" the old woman continued to persuade.
But the old man just smiled without saying a word.
The old woman helplessly shook her head, 
went back home to get her luggage, joined the group going up the mountain, 
and left the old man alone at home.

[P7] The cold wind howled, and the sky grew darker and darker.
At midnight, 'Nian' roared and burst into the village.
'Nian' vaguely sensed that the atmosphere in the village was different. It looked up and saw that at the old woman's doorstep, there were big red papers pasted.
It glanced at them, and its body actually trembled, letting out a strange cry.

[P8] "Nian" quickly turned its gaze away and looked inside the house.
To its surprise, the house was filled with lit candles, glowing with light.
This brightness deeply stung "Nian"'s eyes.

"Nian" thought: "What trick is this family playing? How dare they mock me!
I'll eat you all!"
Then, it glared, roared, and lunged forward.

[P9] "Peng li pa la!"
Too slow to speak, too fast to act.
The old man inside lit a string of firecrackers and threw them out.
The firecrackers drew a beautiful arc in the air, landing perfectly
on the head of the 'Nian'.
"Peng li pa la!"
Just as the 'Nian' was about to burst through the door, the firecrackers exploded above its head.
A wave of pain hit it, and thick smoke obscured its eyes.

[P10] "Nian" saw the red color and trembled all over.
It realized the situation was bad, stumbled three steps at a time, and fled in a panic.
"Nian" jumped in fright and dared not charge forward.
When the thick smoke cleared, it found the door had opened.
"Hahaha..." Standing in the courtyard was an old man wearing a bright red robe,
laughing loudly.

[P11] The villagers were overjoyed, putting on new clothes,
and new hats, visiting relatives and friends to greet each other with joy.
On the first day of the New Year, people returned from the mountains.
To everyone's surprise, everything in the village
was intact and undamaged.

[P12] At this moment, the old woman remembered the beggar's words,
and suddenly understood.
She told the villagers about it, and everyone found it
very magical.

People rushed to the old woman's house to see what had happened.
They found red paper pasted on her door.
Inside, the house was filled with glowing red candles. In the yard, there was still a pile
of unburned firecrackers, crackling "pap-pap".

[P13] "It seems that 'Nian' is afraid of red."
"That's right, it's also afraid of light!"
"The sound of firecrackers can drive it away!"
Everyone discussed and found a way to drive away 'Nian'.
From then on, every New Year's Eve, every household would paste red couplets on their doors,
and set off loud firecrackers at the door.
Good luck and prosperity
Five lakes and four seas are all spring colors
Ten thousand rivers and a thousand mountains are all

[P14] On New Year's Eve, families gather together,
eat the New Year's Eve dinner, light candles at home, and keep them burning all night.
The light makes the house bright, and the 'Nian' monster dares not come anymore.
On the first day of the New Year, people visit relatives and friends, exchange New Year greetings,
and convey their wishes and blessings.
Later, these customs spread widely and evolved into the
most lively and grandest festival in Chinese folk culture: the Spring Festival.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《过年的传说》的封面，展示了书名、作者、出版社信息以及一只被鞭炮吓到的怪兽形象，暗示了故事主题。
[P2] 本页介绍了传说中的怪兽“年”，描述了它恐怖的外形和每到除夕便从海底爬上岸、使大地震动的习性。
[P3] 本页描绘了怪兽“年”上岸后疯狂吞噬生命，人们因此惊恐万分，纷纷逃往深山老林躲避的情景。
[P4] 本页描绘了除夕夜桃花村的乡亲们因害怕怪兽“年”而纷纷收拾行李、上山避难的场景，同时一个神秘的乞讨老人出现在村外。
[P5] 一位老婆婆给村外的乞讨老人送食物，并劝他上山避难，老人却自信表示若能留宿一晚，他定能把怪兽“年”赶跑。
[P6] 老婆婆劝说乞讨老人躲避怪兽“年”，但老人笑而不语，最终老婆婆无奈离开，留下老人独自在家。
[P7] 除夕夜，怪兽“年”闯入村庄，发现老婆婆家门口贴着大红纸，感到害怕并发出怪叫。
[P8] 怪兽“年”被屋内烛光刺痛眼睛，心生愤怒，决定冲进屋内将里面的人全部吃掉。
[P9] 除夕夜，怪兽“年”闯入村庄，屋里的老人点燃鞭炮扔向它，鞭炮在“年”的头顶炸开，浓烟遮住了它的双眼，使其痛苦不堪。
[P10] 怪兽“年”被鞭炮的浓烟和红色吓到，惊慌逃走，发现门已打开，院中一位身穿红袍的老人正大笑，显得毫不畏惧。
[P11] 大年初一，村民们从山上回来，发现村庄完好无损，大家高兴地穿上新衣，互相拜年道喜。
[P12] 大年初一，村民们回到村庄，发现老婆婆家门上贴着红纸，屋内点满红蜡烛，院中鞭炮仍在响，大家对此感到惊奇。
[P13] 村民们发现怪兽“年”害怕红色、光和鞭炮声，于是总结出驱赶它的方法，并在除夕夜开始贴红对联、放鞭炮，以庆祝新年。
[P14] 本页描绘了除夕夜家人团聚吃年夜饭、点灯烛的温馨场景，并解释了这些习俗如何演变成春节，以及大年初一走亲访友的传统。
